tools.name: search_venues
tools.description: Use this when the guest wants a hotel, restaurant or attraction in a place, e.g. 'a quiet hotel near Chaweng Beach' or 'seafood in Bophut'. Results are sorted by distance when you give `near`. Don't use this when you already have a venue_id: call get_venue. Results come in pages of 10: when more_res

tools.name: get_venue
tools.description: Use this when the guest is interested in one venue: its rooms, tables or tickets, from-prices, opening times, policies and how it answers requests. Don't use this to find venues: call search_venues.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Use this when the guest wants to know whether a room, table or ticket is free before sending a request. Answers available, unavailable or unknown. Unknown means the venue keeps no calendar with ATAbooking: the guest can still send_lead and the venue answers. Don't use this to hold anything: nothing

tools.name: send_lead
tools.description: Use this when the guest has chosen a venue and wants it to get in touch: it forwards their request (dates, party, contact, message) to the venue at once. It is a request, not a booking: nothing is held or paid, and the venue contacts the guest directly. Check the details with the guest before callin

tools.name: get_lead_status
tools.description: Use this when the guest asks whether the venue has received their request. Shows each channel's delivery state (portal, email, WhatsApp, webhook). It doesn't show whether the venue has accepted: the venue answers the guest directly. Needs the status_token send_lead returned.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_lead" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_venue, check_availability, send_lead, get_lead_status · Private data: send_lead · Public sink: send_lead, get_lead_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_venue, check_availability, send_lead, get_lead_status · Private data: send_lead · Public sink: send_lead, get_lead_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_availability" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
